detailed_description: GIF Maker turns two or more uploaded images into a browser-generated animated GIF. Add image frames, reorder or remove frames, set the frame delay in milliseconds, choose the GIF quality setting, and decide whether the animation should loop forever. The tool centers each frame on a canvas sized to the largest uploaded image, uses a white background, previews the generated result, and downloads the finished file as a GIF. It is designed for quick image-sequence animations; it does not trim media, change frame dimensions, add text layers, or process videos.
usage_steps: Click the upload area and select two or more image files.
Use the frame arrows to move images earlier or later in the sequence, or remove frames you do not need.
Set frame delay in milliseconds to control the animation speed.
Adjust the quality slider; lower values produce higher quality with larger files.
Choose whether the GIF should loop forever.
Click Create GIF, preview the result, then download the generated animation.
usage_examples: Create a simple before-and-after animation from two screenshots.
Turn a few product photos into a looping preview for a draft post.
Combine diagram frames into a short educational animation.
Make a quick UI walkthrough from exported image frames.

faqs.question: How many images do I need?
faqs.answer: You need at least two frames before the Create GIF button appears.

faqs.question: Can I reorder frames?
faqs.answer: Yes. Use the arrow buttons on each frame thumbnail to move it earlier or later.

faqs.question: How are different frame sizes handled?
faqs.answer: No. The output canvas uses the largest uploaded width and height, and smaller frames are centered on a white background.

faqs.question: Can it process movie files?
faqs.answer: No. The current tool creates GIFs from uploaded image files, not from movie files.
